full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned order dated 14-3-2017 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 arising out of Succession Case. No. 534 of 2015 so far it relates to the direction directing the parties to attend the Forensic DNA Profiling Department of Dhaka Medial College Hospital for testing DNA of the parties should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Shorn of unnecessary details, facts of the case lies in a very short compos. The petitioner Nos. 1-4 as sons and daughters of deceased Abdul Khaleque and the petitioner Nos. 5 and 6 wife and mother of the deceased respectively filed Succession Certificate Case No. 534 of 2015 praying for issuance of a succession certificate. The Joint District Judge 3rd court, Dhaka, issued succession certified to the petitioners on 17-6-2015. The opposite party No.1 as applicant filed Revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 on 12-8-2015 praying for cancellation of the succession certificate issued to the petitioners claiming that he is one of the sons by second wife of Abdul Khaleque. The learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka heard the case ex parte on 6-6-2016 and allowing Revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 cancelled the succession certificate issued to the petitioners. On coming to know the fact, the petitioner filed an application before the learned Joint District Judge on 5-9-2016 praying for recalling the order No. 13 dated 6-6-2016. The learned Joint District Judge heard the application and on contested hearing by its order No. 19 dated 14-3-2017 allowed the application filed by the petitioner and restored the Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 in its original number and position, but passed an order suo moto directing the parties to deposit an amount of Taka 10,000 as fee for DNA test and directed the petitioner No. 1 and the opposite party to be present before the Forensic Department, Dhaka Medical College and Hospital on 11-6-2017. 

 5. Mr Abdullah Al Mubin, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the order of the trial court is not based on correct and legal position of law as neither the petitioner nor the opposite party filed any application before the court below to determine parentage of the opposite party by DNA test. He further submits that the court cannot order blood test as a matter of course without facing any difficulty from the evidences adduced before it by both the parties. But in the instant case neither the petitioner nor the opposite party adduced any evidence in support of their respective cases both oral and documentary. As such, at this stage, unless the parties to this proceeding prayed for determining the parentage of the opposite party by DNA test, the court below cannot pass any order suo moto directing the parties to give sample of blood for analysis. 

 6. Mr Mubin further submits that section 112 of the Evidence Act provides that if a person was born during the continuance of a valid marriage between his mother and any man or within two hundred and eighty days after its dissolution and the mother remains unmarried, it shall be taken as conclusive proof that he is the legitimate son of the man, unless it can be shown that the parties to the marriage had no access to each other at any time when he could have been begotten in order to succeed in the succession application the applicant has to adduce cogent and credible evidence in support of the application. But the court below before adducing evidence by both the parties and without finding any difficulty to determine the dispute in question most illegally passed the order directing for DNA test of the petitioner No. 1 and the opposite party and, as such, the order is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions he has referred to the case of Shri Banarsi Doss vs Mrs Teeku Dutta, reported in 4 SCC 449. 

 7. Mr Mohammad Nazrul Islam, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1 submits that the court below passed the order for DNA test considering urgency of the matter as the petitioner after obtaining succession certificate from the court trying to dispose of the properties left by Md Abdul Khaleque depriving the opposite party from his legitimate claim as one of the sons of late Abdul Khaleque. He further submits that the order itself has not caused any loss to the parties to the proceeding, moreso, it will ensure the claim of the parties to the proceeding and will help the court for proper adjudication of the matter in dispute. He further submits that the petitioner raised objection that the opposite party is not the son of late Md Abdul Khaleque that is why the court directed for DNA test for determining the parentage of the opposite party and, as such, the courts below has not committed any error or legality in passing, the order. In support of his submission he has referred to the case of Sadashiv Mallikarjun Kheradkar vs Smt. Nandini Sadashiv Kheradkar, reported in 1996(1) Bombay CR 454. 

 9. From perusal of impugned judgment and order it appears that the order passed by the court below in fact on the basis of an application filed by the petitioner praying for recalling the order passed ex parte cancelling the succession certificate issued in favour of the petitioner in Succession Certificate Case No. 534 of 2015. The court below upon contested hearing allowed the said application and recalled its order dated 6-6-2016 passed in revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 cancelling the succession certificate issued on 17-6-2016. But at the end of the order the court below directed both the parties to the proceeding to deposit Taka 10,000, 5,000 each and two passport size photograph duly attested to be submitted before the forensic medicine laboratory for DNA test on 15.11.2016 without any prayer from any party of the proceeding. It is also appeared that the court below did not give any reasoning why DNA test of the opposite party No. 1 and petitioner No. 1 is at all required for the purpose of disposal of the proceeding before it. The claims of the opposite party is that he is one of the son of late Md Abdul Khaleque by his second Wife and the petitioner without making him pally to the succession certificate proceeding obtained the certificate for which he filed revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2016. The matter before the court below is still pending. The applicant of the revocation miscellaneous case has ample opportunity to prove his claim before the court below by producing documentary evidences and adducing oral evidences. But that process is still pending before the court below. In order to succeed in the succession application as well as in revocation application both the parties have to adduce required evidences in support of their respective claims before the trial court. And after adducing evidences by the parties to the proceeding if the trial court feels it difficult to come into a conclusion or if it find that the evidences are not sufficient or relevant for the purpose of adjudication of the matter in dispute, then it can order for DNA test for the purpose of determining the dispute between the parties. DNA test is not to be directed as a matter of routine and it can be directed only in deserving cases where such a direction is necessary for proper adjudication of the matter in dispute. Present case does not at its present stage fall to that category. I am, therefore, not at all inclined to express any opinion on the merit of the case relating to succession application but I think that the justice will be done if the court below is directed to dispose of the case expeditiously considering urgency of the matter. 

 12. The impugned order dated 14-3-2017 passed by the learned Joint District Judge 3rd Court, Dhaka in Revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 so far it relates to the direction directing the parties to attend the forensic DNA test profiling department of Dhaka Medial College Hospital for testing DNA is hereby set aside. The court below is hereby directed to dispose of the revocation Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2015 within a shortest possible time
